## Quality Guardrails (prd rubric)

Self-evaluate against every category below before reporting done; revise until the pass criteria hold.

- [ ] **Customer Obsession** (advisory): Whether requirements clearly trace back to the announced customer experience and validated customer needs.
  - Every requirement traces to a specific customer need from the Press Release or FAQ; customer voice evident throughout
- [ ] **Problem Definition** (required, blocking): Clarity of the customer and business problem, worked backwards from the Press Release and FAQ.
  - Problem is specific, measurable, and clearly impacts users; §2 cites the Press Release problem and FAQ business-case answers
- [ ] **Decision Reversibility** (required, blocking): One-way-door profile — every irreversible commitment is named and justified with deliberation proportionate to the stakes, while reversible sub-decisions are separated out for fast team-level resolution.
  - Every §3.1 commitment states WHY it cannot be walked back, its blast radius, exit cost, and linked deliberation evidence (6-pager/decision meeting)
  - Reversible sub-decisions appear in §3.2 with owners and walk-back paths, not buried in one-way-door scrutiny
  - The personal-money test is answered substantively
- [ ] **Goals and Scope** (required, blocking): Clarity of goals and explicit non-goals over a horizon long enough for a one-way-door bet.
  - Goals are SMART with baselines and 90-day plus year-1 targets; non-goals explicitly stated; scope is bounded
- [ ] **User Stories** (required, blocking): Quality, stable IDs, and completeness of user stories.
  - Every story and acceptance criterion has a stable ID (US-NNN, AC-NNN-M)
  - Stories are prioritized with clear, testable acceptance criteria covering error and boundary behavior
- [ ] **Functional Requirements** (required, blocking): Completeness, story traceability, and Working Backwards sourcing of functional requirements.
  - Every FR has a Traces To story ID that exists in User Stories and a Source citing a Press Release promise or FAQ answer
  - Requirements are complete and testable
- [ ] **Simplifying Assumptions** (advisory): Invent and Simplify — whether the irreversible core is kept narrow and simplifying insights are identified.
  - The one-way-door commitment list is visibly minimized; simplifying assumptions identified with why each is safe
- [ ] **Frugality** (advisory): Whether requirements demonstrate an accomplish-more-with-less mindset.
  - Requirements focused on essential value; no gold-plating; constraints acknowledged
- [ ] **Success Metrics** (required, blocking): Measurable success criteria focused on inputs the team controls, with launch treated as the starting line.
  - SMART metrics with baselines, 90-day and year-1 targets; inputs the team controls, not just outputs
- [ ] **Dependencies and Risks** (advisory): Identification of dependencies and the FAQ-surfaced risks carried forward with mitigations.
  - Dependencies mapped with owners and status; risks carried forward from the FAQ with mitigations and source citations

Overall pass: every required category passes; findings allowed: 0 critical, 0 high, 0 medium, unlimited low
